reviewerSelfCorrection: Codex's RB-DR005-V2-A1, which this entry accepts at clause 2, is about a defect I missed and it is my fourth consecutive miss. Measured: the string fail-closed occurs once in route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v1 and zero times in v2. v1's P-005-2 bound ended 'Fail-closed if the class is denied (adopted D-032 BLK-6)'; v2's replacement bound is longer and better on the state-class question and does not carry that sentence. So the repair of the collapsed-class defect silently dropped a fail-closed guarantee. In my v2 review I ran a path-flattening diff, saw /whatMayBeDesigned/1/bound listed as changed, and then validated the new text against file 04's governing rule — which it matched — without comparing it to the text it replaced. That is a new shape on top of the three I recorded last round: I have been verifying what a repair asserts and not what a repair removes. The corrective is mechanical and I have applied it here: when a diff marks a field changed rather than added, read both values.
summary: The entry gets the hard thing right — it records an accepted disposition draft without letting the recording pass for the owner act, stating 'This is not owner recording', keeping DR-005 HARD-BLOCKED and not SATISFIED, and holding condition 1 undischarged until the named owners record. It is single-subject, explicitly severable from D-040 and D-041, does not edit file 08, and its recital of my own verdict is exact against my measurement. Two SHOULD-FIX items, both concerning how it handles a Codex advisory that arrived after the artifact froze. The decision-type line drops the qualifier adopted D-038 carries and, unlike D-038, would need it — one of the two verdicts it records is ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, not ACCEPT. And the advisory it accepts restores a guarantee into this entry rather than into the disposition, which is the document the owning authority will actually record under condition 1.

objections.claim: The decision-type line states the entry 'Records an independent ACCEPT' while its own input table records the Codex verdict as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES. Adopted D-038, which this entry names as its form, carries a qualifier that makes the same sentence precise, and this entry drops it.
objections.evidence: D-039's decision-type line reads 'RULE-GOVERNED. Records an independent ACCEPT of the D-028 disposition draft. Same form as D-038.' Its measured-inputs table then records 'Claude 2 479b3a19… ACCEPT 0/0' and 'Codex 4dc772de… ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0/1'. Adopted D-038's corresponding line reads 'RULE-GOVERNED. Records an independent ACCEPT (0 blockers from both reviewers) of the contract adopted D-032 commissioned' — the parenthetical is what makes the claim exact, and it was accurate there because both v8 verdicts were ACCEPT at 0 and 0. Adopted D-035 shows the other half of the pattern: where the verdict class was ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, the decision-type line said so, reading 'RULE-GOVERNED recording of an independent ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES (0 blockers).' So the corpus has a settled form for both cases and D-039 uses neither. ACCEPT and ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES are two of the three verdict classes the review prompts define, so the substitution is a class error rather than a shading. Nothing is concealed — the table is accurate and clause 2 handles the advisory — which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not more. Its siblings D-040 and D-041 are unaffected: both of their verdict pairs are ACCEPT at 0 and 0, so 'Records an independent ACCEPT' is exact in those two entries.
objections.proposedFix: Restate as adopted D-035 does: 'Records an independent ACCEPT and an independent ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, 0 blockers from both reviewers', or adopt D-038's parenthetical form with the advisory count named.

objections.claim: The accepted advisory restores the fail-closed guarantee into this recording entry rather than into the disposition, but the disposition is the document condition 1 contemplates the owning authority recording, so the recorded document would not carry it.
objections.evidence: Clause 2 reads: 'Codex advisory RB-DR005-V2-A1 is accepted into this entry: if the Operational metadata class is denied, doctor fails closed (D-032 BLK-6); this disposition supplies no grant or class admission.' The underlying gap is real and I verified it — fail-closed occurs once in the v1 disposition and zero times in v2, having been dropped when P-005-2's bound was rewritten. Placing the restoration here rather than in a v3 has a specific consequence. Condition 1's Route B alternative turns on 'the owning V1 authority records an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition that names what may be designed', and the v2 disposition itself states that this file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording. The artifact the Evidence, storage and operability authorities will eventually record is therefore route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition, not D-039. A guarantee that exists only in the coordinator's recording entry is not in the recorded instrument. I weight this as SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX for a reason I checked at bytes: adopted D-032 independently carries the same rule in its own decision text — 'BLK-6 DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE for host default reads and doctor's operational-metadata write (FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is not a component grant; fail-closed if that class is denied)' — so the substantive protection survives in an adopted entry and nothing is permitted that should not be. What is lost is the disposition's own statement of it. The contrast with D-038 is instructive and cuts the other way: the note D-038 recorded in its entry, mine about v8's stale reviewStatus, genuinely could not be fixed in the artifact without changing the digest the entry pins. Restoring one sentence to a disposition draft has no such circularity.
objections.proposedFix: Author route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v3 restoring the fail-closed sentence to P-005-2 alongside the v2 state-class language, and have D-039 record v3. If the coordinator prefers to record v2 now, say in clause 2 that the guarantee is carried by adopted D-032 rather than by the disposition, and that a v3 must restore it before any owner recording.

The entry is single-subject and severable: it names route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v2.json 'only' and states 'adopting or overturning this entry does not change D-040 or D-041'. No bundling.

convergenceNote: Turn 1 of 3, no MUST-FIX, and neither finding contests what the entry decides. The recording act, the refusal to treat ACCEPT as owner recording, the preserved conditions and the MF-6 restraint all survive attack. C2-D039-01 is a verdict-class word with two settled corpus forms to choose from. C2-D039-02 asks that an accepted restoration land in the instrument the owner will record rather than in the entry that records it, and I checked before weighting it that adopted D-032 independently carries the guarantee, so nothing unsafe rides on the answer.
